description: Intelligence is one of the six scored hero attributes; its name is a value of attribute.attribute_name and its ratings occupy the same value scale as the other five traits.
Strength is one of the six scored hero attributes, distinguished only by its name value in attribute.attribute_name.
Speed is one of the six scored hero attributes, distinguished only by its name value in attribute.attribute_name.
Durability is one of the six scored hero attributes, distinguished only by its name value in attribute.attribute_name.
Power is one of the six scored hero attributes, distinguished only by its name value in attribute.attribute_name.
Combat is one of the six scored hero attributes, distinguished only by its name value in attribute.attribute_name.

connection_condition: superhero.eye_colour_id references colour.id, so eye colour values are drawn from the shared colour vocabulary
description: Eye colour is one of the three hero colour aspects that draw their values from the single colour vocabulary; this shared domain is what allows colour values to be compared across positions.

connection_condition: superhero.hair_colour_id references colour.id, so hair colour values are drawn from the shared colour vocabulary
description: Hair colour shares the same colour vocabulary as eye and skin colour, so an equal value in two positions means the same colour.

connection_condition: superhero.skin_colour_id references colour.id, so skin colour values are drawn from the shared colour vocabulary
description: Skin colour shares the same colour vocabulary as eye and hair colour; it is the position most often left as the 'No Colour' placeholder.

connection_condition: superhero.publisher_id references publisher.id; a few heroes have no publisher reference
description: Each hero is published by one publisher, so a publisher groups and accounts for the heroes it owns.

connection_condition: hero_power links superhero.id to superpower.id in a many-to-many relationship
description: A hero possesses zero or more named abilities, and the same ability is shared by many heroes; the ability vocabulary exists independently of any hero.
Each hero carries one gender classification used as a filtering dimension.
Each hero carries one species or origin classification used as a filtering dimension.

connection_condition: superhero.alignment_id references alignment.id; a few heroes have no alignment reference
description: Each hero carries one moral alignment classification.

connection_condition: hero_attribute.hero_id references superhero.id; a hero-trait rating cannot exist without its hero
description: A hero's scored traits are component measurements of that hero: each rating belongs to exactly one hero, and heroes without ratings simply have none of these components.

connection_condition: hero_attribute pairs attribute_id with attribute_value in the same row
description: A rating value is a component of one hero-attribute measurement; it has no meaning apart from the trait it scores.

connection_condition: attribute.attribute_name and superpower.power_name are two independent vocabularies; the names 'Intelligence' and 'Durability' occur in both, and 'Super Speed' and 'Super Strength' echo attribute names
description: Scored traits and named abilities are two separate trait systems describing a hero. Words such as speed, strength, intelligence and durability appear in both vocabularies, so they must never be treated as the same measure.
A percentage share is derived from two hero counts taken on the same population: the subgroup count divided by the population count, scaled to a percentage.
A count difference is derived from two hero counts taken on a comparable population by subtracting one from the other.
Colour popularity is derived by counting heroes per colour value within a population and ordering those counts from most to least common.
